messages:
Luis (Support): FYI escalation from Avery (customer). They report sudden surge of 429s for /v1/generate starting ~09:12 UTC after a marketing blast. They say traffic spiked to 6k QPS for a 5QPS plan 😬
Maya (SRE): details plz — headers/trace id or sample request? 429 body?
Luis (Support): Pasting shortened customer report + sample response:

Avery (Customer): "We started a campaign at 09:07 UTC. Between 09:10-09:18 we saw lots of 429 responses saying 'quota exceeded'. We were under our expected burst but still got rate-limited. Sample response: { \"error\": \"RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED\", \"limit\": 5000, \"remaining\": 0, \"reset\": 1678902340 }"

Luis (Support): Attached logs from proxy (redacted) show a lot of 429s with header X-Request-ID: req_7b9c. I forwarded traces to Sam.
Sam (Runtime): I pulled request traces for req_7b9c and surrounding window. Observations: token-bucket per-tenant refill rate looks correct, but there are bursts of concurrent connections from multiple IPs that hit our burst-cap enforcement layer. The limiter service reports lots of "leaky-bucket overflow" errors at 09:11.
Maya (SRE): Oof. Could be two things: 1) config mismatch between global quota and per-route QPS (we recently rolled per-route overrides) 2) state desync between tokens stored in redis shards leading to undercounted tokens.
Sam (Runtime): I checked active config: QA shows per-tenant burst = 1000 tokens, refill = 500 tokens/s. Customer's contract says burst=3000, refill=1500. Looks like the per-tenant contract didn't propagate to production due to a rollout rule bug (PR 5132). The rollout rolled back but the flag remained set for some services.
Maya (SRE): That would explain "they were under expected burst". Is there a solid repro? can we replay traffic?
Luis (Support): Customer gave sample replay (anonymized). I can run it against our staging limiter if needed.
Sam (Runtime): Please hold on replay — we should first mitigate prod: temporary mitigation options: a) increase tenant quota for Avery to match contract b) enable permissive bypass for their token in limiter c) rollback the rollout flags to previous known-good. I can patch 2 quickly but need approval.
Rebecca (Acct Mgmt): We need to keep customer online ASAP. I'm OK with temporary bypass while you fix. Avery is on an enterprise reserved plan. @Maya please prioritize.
Maya (SRE): On it. I'm applying a temporary increases for tenant-id: t-9843. Command I'm running: 

```bash
# increase burst to 3000 and refill to 1500 for tenant t-9843
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" \
  https://internal-api.redwood/v1/admin/quotas/t-9843 \
  -d '{"burst":3000,"refill":1500}'
```

Maya (SRE): Applied. I also set a 30m TTL rollback for the change. Watching metrics.
ratebot: [09:28 UTC] limiter-service.alert: high_429_rate tenant=t-9843 count=8200 window=5m :rotating_light:
Maya (SRE): After the change, host metrics show 429s dropping immediately. Customer confirms degraded traffic is passing now.
Avery (Customer): thanks, that fixed it. We still saw higher latencies but no 429s. appreciate the fast follow-up.
Sam (Runtime): Root cause summary so far: rollout PR 5132 introduced a bug where per-tenant configs were shadowed by a default override when the feature flag was partially rolled out. In some hot paths the override zeros the burst value, effectively making the tenant use the global conservative quotas.
Maya (SRE): Action items:
- Sam to open emergency patch to avoid override when tenant config exists (PR 5198)
- Sam to add unit/integration test to simulate partial flag state
- Ops to add a grace-period metric: "config-mismatch-rate" alert if tenant-config != effective-config
- Support to notify customer with timeline & RCA

Sam (Runtime): PR 5198 opened: https://git.redwood/infra/5198 (hotfix branch). Will cut canary to 3 hosts then full rollout after 30m if green.
Maya (SRE): Also discovered a secondary issue: our redis shard had intermittent network hiccups causing delayed token writes; added read-repair to limiter in hotfix v0.9.3.
Luis (Support): I'll draft a customer note: temporary quota bump + hotfix + monitoring change. Reply required: please include timestamp window + confirmation of TTL rollback behavior.
Rebecca (Acct Mgmt): I'll coordinate billing note — we should not charge for throttled requests. I'll route to billing to ensure credits if needed.
Sam (Runtime): Rolling out hotfix to canary now: 
ratebot: [09:52 UTC] deploy-bot: deploy started infra/limiter v0.9.3 -> canary (3 hosts)
Maya (SRE): Canary looks good, 0 errors for 20m, proceeding to full rollout.
ratebot: [10:02 UTC] deploy-bot: deploy completed infra/limiter v0.9.3 -> prod (all hosts)
Maya (SRE): Post-deploy checks green. Reverting the temporary TTL bump now (removing permissive bypass). Running rollback command: 

```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" \
  https://internal-api.redwood/v1/admin/quotas/t-9843/rollback
```

Maya (SRE): Rollback completed at 10:08 UTC. No spike in 429s. Monitoring for 2h.
Avery (Customer): Confirmed normal behavior, thanks for quick fix and the follow-up.
Luis (Support): Customer-facing RCA draft attached and sent. Link: internal:/r/1953007777/rca-draft.md
Sam (Runtime): Follow-ups (owners):
- Sam: PR 5198 -> merged, ensure tests. (done)
- Maya: add "config-mismatch-rate" alert (PR 5201)
- Ops: run redis shard health checks daily for next 7 days
- Support: confirm customer credit eligibility

Maya (SRE): Closing thread once billing & billing credit confirmed. Thanks everyone. :clap:
Luis (Support): Adding final note: learned - partial rollout + default override + transient redis issues = real pain. We'll update runbook to include immediate quota bump pattern and TTL policy.
